title: A Definition of Catastrophic Performance
abstract: arXiv:2611.06219v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A central challenge in AI is specifying objectives that align with human preferences. While existing theoretical results elucidate how misspecification impacts performance, they typically do not distinguish between merely suboptimal and catastrophic outcomes. To enable rigorous analysis of catastrophic risk from AI misalignment, we introduce a formal definition of catastrophic performance. Our definition is based on two reference values. The first, baseline value, captures the value attained if no agent is deployed. The second, orthogonal value, captures the value of a trajectory that is unrelated to human preferences, in a sense we describe. Orthogonal value is typically far worse than baseline value. We interpret these reference values through examples in which past human activity has altered the state of the environment to human benefit. translated_abstract: 人工智能的一个核心挑战是制定与人类偏好相一致的目标。虽然现有的理论结果阐明了目标设定错误如何影响性能，但它们通常没有区分仅仅是次优的结果与灾难性的结果。为了能够对人工智能目标错位带来的灾难性风险进行严格分析，我们引入了灾难性性能的正式定义。我们的定义基于两个参考值：第一个是基线值，表示如果没有部署任何智能体时所获得的价值；第二个是正交值，表示一条在我们所描述意义上与人类偏好无关的轨迹的价值。正交值通常远差于基线值。我们通过一些例子来阐释这些参考值，在这些例子中，过去的人类活动已经改变了环境状态并使其有利于人类。从由此产生的状态出发，部署一个以加速进一步……
tldr: 该论文提出了“灾难性性能”的正式定义，通过基线值和正交值两个参考值来区分次优结果与灾难性结果，从而为严格分析人工智能目标错位带来的灾难性风险提供了理论基础。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a formal definition of catastrophic performance based on two reference values (baseline value and orthogonal value), enabling rigorous analysis of catastrophic risks from AI misalignment by distinguishing catastrophic outcomes from merely suboptimal ones.
